Dodai
DOH-dye
proper noun
Hebrew doday, “beloved” or “loving,” an Ahohite, captain of the second monthly course of David’s host, the father of Eleazar the mighty man.

📖 Biblical Definition

Dodai the Ahohite, also called Dodo, was set over the course of the second month in the ordering of David’s army, of four and twenty thousand men (1Ch 27:4). He was the father of Eleazar, one of the three mightiest of David’s men, who smote the Philistines until his hand was weary and clave unto the sword, so that the LORD wrought a great victory that day (2Sa 23:9). His name signifies “beloved,” and he stood high among the valiant, both for his own captaincy and for the renown of the son he begat. The dictionary honours that Dodai held his appointed month in the host, taking his place in the ordered ranks that David set in their courses; for the kingdom of the anointed was no rabble of warriors but a host marshalled under the head. There is a sweetness in his name, beloved, that befits the company of the king, for these mighty men loved David and hazarded their lives for him in the day of his distress. Dodai stands as a witness that to be beloved and to be faithful go together in the service of the king, and that the love which the saints bear to Christ the greater David is proved in steadfast service in the rank He appoints. The father who served in his course begat a son who clave unto the sword; so a faithful generation passes on its valour, and the LORD is glorified in both.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

An Ahohite, captain of the second monthly course of David’s host, and father of Eleazar the mighty man.

expand to see more

DODAI, an Ahohite, also called Dodo, a captain in the host of David.

He was set over the course of the second month, of four and twenty thousand men.

He was the father of Eleazar, one of the three mightiest of David’s men.

His son Eleazar smote the Philistines until his hand clave unto the sword.

It witnesses to faithful service and a valiant generation under the king.

📖 Key Scripture

1Ch 27:4 — "And over the course of the second month was Dodai an Ahohite, and of his course was Mikloth also the ruler: in his course likewise were twenty and four thousand."

2Sa 23:9 — "And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away:"

1Co 16:13 — "Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong."

Psa 18:39 — "For thou hast girded me with strength unto the battle: thou hast subdued under me those that rose up against me."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A man of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; he witnesses to faithful service and a valiant generation under the king.

expand to see more

Dodai the Ahohite is a man of the sacred record, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine him. The dictionary records him that the reader who meets the name among David’s captains may know him for a real soldier in a real host, who kept his appointed month and begat a son mighty in the day of battle.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that love for the king and faithful service in his rank go together, and that a valiant father may beget a valiant son. He whose name means beloved held his course in David’s host and gave to Israel an Eleazar whose hand clave unto the sword. The saint who would pass on a heritage of faithfulness may remember Dodai, and serve Christ the greater David in the station appointed, that a faithful generation may follow.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “beloved,” Dodai names an Ahohite captain in David’s host.

Dodai — Hebrew doday, “beloved” or “loving.”

He is also called Dodo the Ahohite in the book of Samuel.

He was set over the course of the second month, of four and twenty thousand.

He was the father of Eleazar, one of the three mightiest of David’s men.

His son clave unto the sword until the LORD wrought a great victory.

Usage

"Like Dodai the beloved, love for the king is proved in steadfast service in the rank he appoints."

"The LORD who girded David’s men with strength raises up valiant sons from faithful fathers."

"A father who keeps his course may beget a son whose hand cleaves unto the sword in the LORD’s battles."
